Subject: Post-call recap & procurement path — next steps

Hi Samantha / Carlos —

Thanks again for taking time today. Short recap from our discovery and a few concrete next steps so procurement can move forward quickly: 

What we heard (summary)
- Primary objective: reduce latency/cost for customer-chat and knowledge-base search while keeping PHI-safe ingestion.
- Procurement preference: prefers PO-based vendor onboarding but is open to Marketplace if it simplifies internal purchase approvals.
- Current runbook: procurement requires vendor form, W9, and SOC2 evidence for new SaaS vendors.

Open questions for Brightside procurement
- Can you confirm whether card payments are acceptable for initial POC spend (< $10k) or do you need a PO for any vendor payment?
- Do you want us to pursue an AWS Marketplace listing to enable procurement to buy without a vendor contract?
- Any internal timing constraints (budget cycle / fiscal approvals) we should know about?

Commercial / packaging notes (high level)
- Hosted (Redwood API): on-demand billing per token; fastest to start; supports card/contract.
- Hosted (commit): 1/12/24 month commit options reduce unit price; best if you can commit upfront via PO.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU capacity, predictable throughput; usually requires a 12+ month commit and is procured via contract + PO.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): enterprise license + integration services; multi-quarter onboarding and enterprise licensing.

Attachments I've included: pricing_options_brightside_v2.xlsx (pricing matrix draft) and Brightside-procurement-checklist.pdf (vendor info we typically provide).

Proposed next steps
1) Samantha: confirm procurement preference (Card for POC? or PO-only) and legal/vendor intake contact.
2) If PO-only: confirm the procurement email and any required vendor forms so we can pre-fill them.
3) Marissa & Connor: I'll loop internal ops to prepare a short pricing matrix and a recommended commercial path (hosted commit -> Dedicated on renewal or direct Dedicated if procurement requires multi-year commit).

I'll follow up with a tailored pricing table and the SOC2 evidence link by tomorrow EOD.

Best,

Thanks Dylan — good summary. A few clarifications from procurement's side: 

1) Payment method: Our policy is PO-first for any vendor. We do allow departmental cards for low-dollar POCs but that requires manager approval and is slower in practice. So please assume PO will be required beyond a $5k pilot.

2) Marketplace: We have an internal preference for Marketplace purchases (AWS & GCP) — it reduces our vendor onboarding burden. If Redwood can be on AWS Marketplace with a metered or subscription SKU, that would be attractive.

3) Commit vs on-demand: Procurement wants to see a simple comparison: 
   - Hosted on-demand (no commitment) — list price, estimated monthly spend for pilot.
   - Hosted commit (6/12/24 mo) — committed units and effective unit price.
   - Dedicated 12-mo commit — what is the minimum GPU/throughput commitment and lead time?
   - Private — ballpark professional services + license fees.

4) Compliance: We need SOC2 Type II and an SLA summary. Please attach SOC2 report URL or next steps to access the auditor package.

Timeline: We are targeting an internal procurement decision by Aug 6. Can you get the spreadsheet with the four rows above and a clear recommend commercial path by Wed EOD?

On a separate note: procurement@brightsidehealth.com is the vendor intake mailbox. I'll forward any forms there.

Thanks — Samantha
Samantha Low
Senior Procurement Manager | Brightside Health
